items.name: Zone — cuff elastic band (top of wrist)
items.what: Top edge of the wrist where the elastic yarn is knitted in. The number is whatever parameter the active Set mode assigns to this zone — laps of elastic when Elastic Yarn Set is selected.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Cuff edge very tight and thick — hard to pull over the hand
More elastic used per glove, more elastic breakage at the edge
high.action: Decrease toward the pattern-card value if the edge feels board-stiff or elastic keeps snapping.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Weak elastic edge — cuff rolls up or lifts away
Edge can unravel after washing
low.action: Increase gradually until the edge holds its shape but still stretches comfortably over the hand.

items.name: Zone — wrist
items.what: Main wrist section value — typically the density (stitch length) of the ribbed cuff area.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tight wrist — hard to put on and take off
Elastic pressure marks on the skin after wear
high.action: Decrease by 1–2 if operators complain the wrist is tight or marks appear.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Cuff slips off the hand during work
Wrist looks floppy and loose
low.action: Increase by 1–2 if gloves fall off or the cuff gapes.

items.name: Zone — back of hand
items.what: Back-of-hand zone value, usually density. The back carries most of the visible shaping of the glove.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff back — poor bending, hand tires quickly
Fabric can crackle or stress when flexed
high.action: Decrease by 1–2 if the back feels board-stiff during wear trials.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Baggy back — wrinkles, poor appearance
Glove slides around on the hand
low.action: Increase by 1–2 if the back looks loose or wrinkled on the hand.

items.name: Zone — thumb
items.what: Thumb zone covering the thumb body and its root. Values here strongly affect grip comfort.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tight thumb — restricted movement, grip weakens
Yarn breaks at the thumb root, webbing stressed
high.action: Decrease by 1–2 if the thumb feels tight or yarn breaks at the root.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Loose thumb — webbing sags and rubs
Holes develop at the thumb root over time
low.action: Increase by 1–2 if the thumb webbing feels loose or wears early.

items.name: Zone — palm
items.what: Palm zone value — usually set slightly looser than the back of the hand so the glove can close around objects.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff palm — poor grip feel, hand fatigues
Glove resists closing around tools
high.action: Decrease by 1–2 if gripping feels stiff.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Baggy palm — fabric bunches when gripping
Poor contact with tools, less dexterity
low.action: Increase by 1–2 if the palm bunches up in the hand.

items.name: Zone — index finger
items.what: Index-finger zone. Finger values should stay in proportion to each other — the drawing is the map of the whole hand.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tight finger — pressure on the nail, stiff fingertip
Visible density step against the neighbouring finger
high.action: Decrease toward the card value; keep the step to the middle finger similar to the original pattern.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Loose wrinkled finger — poor dexterity
Tip folds when gripping small parts
low.action: Increase toward the card value in steps of 1.

items.name: Zone — middle finger
items.what: Middle-finger zone — the longest finger, so it carries the highest value in the set (54).

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Visible density step between the fingers
Middle finger stiff, glove looks uneven on the hand
high.action: Decrease while keeping it the highest of the four finger values.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Middle finger sags — glove looks misshaped
Tip short or loose compared with the spec
low.action: Increase back toward 54; it should stay above ring and little finger.

items.name: Zone — ring finger
items.what: Ring-finger zone — normally matches or sits near the index finger value.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tight ring finger — discomfort and stiff tip
Mismatch against index finger if set higher
high.action: Decrease toward the card value, keeping it in line with the index finger.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Loose ring finger — wrinkles, poor fit
low.action: Increase toward the card value in steps of 1.

items.name: Zone — little finger
items.what: Little-finger zone — the smallest finger, so it carries the lowest value (42). The finger selector at the top of the machine screen refers to this zone.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Little finger stiff and out of proportion with the spec
Density step visible against the ring finger
high.action: Decrease toward 42; the little finger should stay clearly the loosest of the four.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Little finger baggy — fabric folds, catches on edges
low.action: Increase toward the card value if the little finger looks loose.

items.name: Tool — Speed Set
items.what: Switches the pattern editor to speed mode — the numbers on the drawing then show the carriage speed for each zone instead of density.

high.title: When to use it
items: Slow down dense or delicate zones — wrist, elastic insert, fingertip reinforcement
Speed up plain zones only after the seam and fingers knit clean at current speed
high.action: After any speed change, run one piece at first-run speed and inspect before full production.

items.name: Tool — Elastic Yarn Set
items.what: Elastic editing mode — set elastic laps and tension per zone. Normally only the cuff zones carry elastic values.

high.title: When to use it
items: Set elastic values on the cuff zones per the order specification
Non-zero elastic on other zones wastes elastic and can pucker the fabric
high.action: Pair elastic changes with the elastic insert and release settings on page 5 for a consistent wrist.

items.name: Tool — Density Set
items.what: Density editing mode — the numbers shown on the drawing (8, 28, 30, 44, 26, 48, 54, 48, 42) are the density values of each zone when this mode is active. Higher number = tighter fabric.

high.title: When to use it
items: Change zone density only for fit corrections requested by QA — a glove too tight or too loose in one zone
Move in steps of 1–2 and re-measure; big jumps show as visible gauge steps on the glove
high.action: Always compare with the pattern card before editing — the card values are the qualified baseline.

items.name: Tool — Sub Yarn Set
items.what: Sub yarn editing mode — assigns the reinforcement (second) yarn to chosen zones, normally palm and/or cuff.

high.title: When to use it
items: Enable on palm and cuff zones only for heavy-duty or cut-resistant orders
Requires sub yarn function ON and sub scissors ON to actually knit
high.action: Match the zones to the order spec sheet — knitting sub yarn where it is not required wastes yarn.

items.name: Tool — Knot Set
items.what: Knot editing mode — controls knotting behaviour per zone for styles that tie off yarn inside the glove.

high.title: When to use it
items: Leave at zero for standard gloves
Use only for the knot styles named in the order specification
high.action: Wrong-zone knotting shows as hard lumps inside the glove — revert to zero if lumps appear.

items.name: Tool — Blow Set
items.what: Air-blow editing mode — sets air blowing per zone to clear lint and cut yarn ends from the knitting area.

high.title: When to use it
items: Keep ON for lint-prone zones — wrist edge and dark yarn jobs
OFF where air disturbs very light yarns or wastes air capacity
high.action: If lint builds up at the wrist edge between pieces, enable blow for the wrist and cuff zones.

items.name: Tool — Head Location
items.what: Fine position offsets of the knitting head per zone — used to align pattern features with the physical needles.

high.title: When this is wrong
items: Pattern features shift a stitch left or right — fingers or seam off-centre
Usually only drifts after head motor, belt or home-sensor service
high.action: Technician / pattern-file value — restore the recorded offsets after any head service; never tune by eye during production.

items.name: Tool — Other Parameters
items.what: Collects the remaining per-zone parameters that do not have their own button — advanced settings grouped for the pattern programmer.

high.title: When to change
items: Only per the pattern documentation for a specific glove style
Random changes here produce defects that are hard to trace — treat this area like a pattern file
high.action: Back up current values before editing; restore immediately if piece quality changes.

items.name: Mitten types — Intact buttons
items.what: The six Intact buttons set each finger and thumb section either closed (Intact) or open with a hole, depending on the glove style being knitted.

high.title: When to use them
items: Set every section to match the style drawing on the order sheet — one wrong section means a full batch of the wrong style
All Intact (current) is correct for standard closed gloves
high.action: After changing any section, run one piece and check every finger against the spec before continuing.

items.name: Mitten laps
items.what: Total number of courses (laps) the machine knits for the mitten-type section when a mitten style is selected. Not used for standard five-finger gloves.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Mitten section too long — proportions wrong, wasted yarn
high.action: Decrease toward the style card value if the section overruns its target length.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Mitten section too short — does not cover the hand as specified
low.action: Increase toward the card value if the section comes up short.

items.name: Density table — row numbers (1–10 here, 11–20 on Next)
items.what: Twenty programmable density segments per bed — rows 1–10 shown on this screen, rows 11–20 on the Next screen. Use Next and Prev to move between the two screens. Each segment defines one row range of the glove and the density knitted inside it.

high.title: How to use the rows
items: Use one row per region that needs its own density — example: wrist rows 40–60 at value 30
Leave unused rows at 0 — the machine ignores them
Program matching regions on Front and Rear unless the style deliberately differs
high.action: Plan the segments on paper from the pattern card before entering them — random entries show as visible density bands on the glove.

items.name: Active row 1 — Front density
items.what: The first two courses of each piece knit at front-bed density 7 — tighter than the surrounding zones, anchoring the cast-on so the start does not ladder.

high.title: Value 7 too HIGH for the start
items: First rows too tight — cast-on edge puckers or curls
Yarn breaks at the very start where tension is already highest
high.action: Decrease toward the zone value if the edge curls or start breaks occur; 7 is mild and usually safe.

low.title: Value 7 too LOW
items: Start rows loose — ladders or open loops at the beginning of the piece
First courses snag during the overlock pass
low.action: Increase toward 7–8 if the first rows look loose compared with the rest of the glove.

items.name: Active row 1 — Rear density
items.what: The same first two courses knit at rear-bed density 10 — noticeably tighter than the front (7), holding the start rows firmly on both beds.

high.title: Value 10 too HIGH for the start
items: Start over-tightened — edge curls toward the back, tension marks
Snapped yarn in the first two courses increases
high.action: Decrease toward 7–8 if you see start-of-piece breaks or a curled edge; keep the rear equal to or slightly above the front.

low.title: Value 10 too LOW
items: Rear start rows looser than front — the piece twists or the cast-on skews
First loops unstable, dropped stitches at the very start
low.action: Increase back toward 10 if the start of the piece skews or twists.

items.name: Why rear 10 differs from front 7
items.what: The rear bed is set 3 density steps tighter than the front for the first two rows — a common start anchor, because the rear bed carries the cast-on and needs the extra hold.

high.title: When the difference is wrong
items: Rear much tighter than this — start curls hard to one side, breaks at cast-on
Rear equal to front — the start can skew or ladder on slippery yarn
high.action: Keep the rear 2–4 steps above the front for these two rows; change both together only if the whole start changes character.

items.name: Button — Delete All
items.what: Clears every Start Row, End Row and Density Value in the table in one action.

high.title: When to use it
items: When switching to a style that needs no table control at all
Before entering a completely new set of segments — safer than editing over old rows
high.action: There is no undo — photograph or write down active rows (like row 1: front 1–2@7, rear 1–2@10) before deleting.

items.name: Button — Copy All
items.what: Copies the Front Density half into the Rear Density half so both beds carry identical segments.

high.title: When to use it
items: After programming the front half, copy then adjust only the rows that must differ — like row 1 here
Also used to return both halves to equal after a trial change
high.action: After copying, re-check rows that are meant to differ — Copy All overwrites them.

items.name: Column — Start Row
items.what: The first course of the piece where this segment density applies.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tightening starts after the target region — the first courses of that region knit at the old, looser density
If set beyond the End Row the segment never activates
high.action: Decrease the Start Row until it lands exactly on the first course of the region; it must be smaller than the End Row.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Density change begins too early — extra courses knit tighter than intended
Yarn breaks or gauge marks appear before the real region starts
low.action: Increase the Start Row to the true first course of the region.

items.name: Column — End Row
items.what: The last course of the piece where this segment density applies. Together with Start Row it brackets the region.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tighter (or looser) knitting continues past the region into the next one
Overlaps the next segment — the transition between regions becomes messy
high.action: Decrease the End Row to the true last course of the region; keep segments non-overlapping.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Region only partly covered — the far end of the zone knits at default density
Visible density step mid-region
low.action: Increase the End Row until the whole region is covered; it must be larger than the Start Row.

items.name: Column — Density Value
items.what: The stitch density knitted between Start Row and End Row. Higher number = tighter fabric, lower = looser.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Fabric in the range very tight — glove fits small there
Yarn breakage rises inside the segment
Visible gauge step against neighbouring regions
high.action: Decrease toward the surrounding zone values — move in steps of 1–2 and re-measure.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Segment knits looser than intended — baggy band, wrinkles
Tension imbalance can drop stitches at the segment edges
low.action: Increase toward the pattern-card value for that region.

items.name: Rows 2–20 are zero — only row 1 is programmed
items.what: Row 1 is the only active segment on this machine: Front knits rows 1–2 of every piece at density 7, Rear knits rows 1–2 at density 10. Every other row is 0 and ignored.

high.title: What this means on the glove
items: Only the first two courses of each piece get table-controlled density — everything after row 2 follows the drawing zone values on page 1
The remaining 19 rows are spare — fill them only if a region needs its own density
high.action: When adding a segment, fill Start Row, End Row and Density Value together — a half-filled row does nothing. Test one piece at first-run speed after any change.

items.name: Front Density vs Rear Density halves
items.what: The left half programs the front bed density, the right half the rear bed density. Both beds knit the same glove, so normally both halves carry identical values.

high.title: When to set them differently
items: Only for styles that deliberately differ face vs back — per the pattern documentation
A difference entered by mistake shows as uneven tension, curling or a misshaped palm
high.action: If in doubt, copy the Front values into the Rear half — equal is the safe default.

items.name: How the table works with the drawing zones
items.what: Wherever a table row is active (non-zero), its Density Value overrides the zone value from the drawing for those rows. Where no row is active, the zone value rules.

high.title: Keep them consistent
items: Do not fight the zones — a table row slightly different from its zone gives a small step; very different gives a visible band
Delete a row by zeroing its three values when the region should follow the zone again
high.action: After editing, knit one piece and flex the region — feel for stiff bands before restarting production.

items.name: Sub yarn table — what it does
items.what: Programs where the reinforcement (sub) yarn is knitted: each row defines a row range (Start Row → End Row), which sub yarn feeder is used (Sub Yarn Number), and whether the yarn ends are locked at the segment boundaries. All values are 0 — the table is inactive, matching sub yarn function OFF.

high.title: How to fill it
items: Fill rows only for orders with reinforced zones — typically palm and/or cuff
Enter Start Row, End Row and Sub Yarn Number together; a half-filled row does nothing
Lock yarn ends at the beginning and end when the tail must not pull out
high.action: Photograph the table before changing it; after any change, knit one piece and check the reinforced zone and the yarn ends.

items.name: Column — Start Row / End Row
items.what: The first and last course of the piece where this sub yarn segment is active — same meaning as in the density table on page 2.

high.title: Rows wrong
items: Start after the zone — reinforcement begins late, the first rows of the zone are single yarn
End before the zone — the tail of the zone is unprotected
Overlapping segments — the feeder switches twice and the overlap knits heavy
high.action: Set Start and End to bracket exactly the zone from the pattern card, and keep segments non-overlapping.

items.name: Column — Sub Yarn Number
items.what: Which sub yarn feeder knits this segment — 1 = first sub yarn, 2 = second (if fitted). 0 = no sub yarn in this row range.

high.title: Value too HIGH / wrong feeder
items: A feeder number the machine does not have fitted → alarms, segment never knits
Wrong feeder on a two-yarn system → the reinforcement uses the wrong yarn and the whole zone fails inspection
high.action: Use 1 for the standard feeder; use 2 only if a second sub yarn system is fitted — check the machine specification first.

low.title: Value 0
items: No reinforcement — correct for standard gloves
Reinforced orders will come out single-yarn if left at 0
low.action: For reinforced orders set the feeder number the spec sheet names, together with Start and End rows.

items.name: Column — Lock Yarn Ends at The Beginning
items.what: Locks (tacks) the sub yarn end at the start of the segment so the tail cannot slip or pull back out. 0 = off, 1 = on.

high.title: Locked (1) when not needed
items: Small tack visible at the segment start
Slightly longer cycle time
high.action: Set 0 when the zone is knitted continuously and the start is captured by surrounding courses.

low.title: Not locked (0) when needed
items: Sub yarn tail works loose after washing or flexing
A loose tail inside the glove irritates the hand and fails inspection
low.action: Set 1 whenever the segment start is a true beginning of sub yarn use, or the order spec asks for locked ends.

items.name: Column — Lock Yarn Ends at The End
items.what: Locks the sub yarn end at the end of the segment — the cut-off tail is secured instead of hanging free.

high.title: Locked (1) when not needed
items: Unnecessary tack and cycle time at the segment end
high.action: Set 0 when the next section continues over the end and captures the tail anyway.

low.title: Not locked (0) when needed
items: Sub yarn end frays or pulls out at the zone boundary
Tail sticks out of the fabric on the inside of the glove
low.action: Set 1 on the last sub yarn segment of the piece and wherever the spec requires secured ends.

items.name: All zeros — sub yarn currently unused
items.what: Every row is 0, so no sub yarn is knitted anywhere — consistent with sub yarn function OFF on page 6 and sub scissors OFF. Standard single-yarn production.

high.title: Before enabling sub yarn anywhere
items: Turn ON sub yarn function and sub scissors, or the table rows will not knit
Check the sub yarn path, tension and scissors cut before the first piece
Enter table rows and zone settings together — one without the other gives no reinforcement
high.action: Run the first reinforced piece at first-run speed and pull-test the reinforced zone and both yarn ends.

items.name: Buttons — Delete All, Aux Set, Sub Sci
items.what: Delete All clears the whole table (no undo — record active rows first). Aux Set opens auxiliary sub yarn parameters (tension and timing of the feeder — technician values). Sub Sci jumps to the sub scissors settings, which must be active for the sub yarn to be cut cleanly.

high.title: When to use each
items: Delete All — when switching to a style with no sub yarn
Aux Set — only with the sub yarn system documentation in hand
Sub Sci — to verify or adjust the cut of the sub yarn ends
high.action: Treat Aux Set values like calibration data: restore recorded values after any feeder service.

items.name: Knot table — what it does
items.what: Programs where knots are tied inside the glove for styles that need them (decorative or functional knots). Each row gives the course where the knot happens (Knot Row), which yarn is tied (Yarn Number), and a fine position offset (Adjustment). All values are 0 — no knots are programmed, matching knotting function 0 on page 7.

high.title: How to use it
items: Fill a row only when the order style calls for a knot at a specific course
Knot Row, Yarn Number and Adjustment work as a set — a half-filled row does nothing
Use Next and Prev to move between the two halves of the table (rows 1–10 and 11–20)
high.action: Photograph the table before changing it; after any change, knit one piece and check the knot sits exactly on the target course.

items.name: Column — Knot Row
items.what: The course (row) of the piece where the knotter ties a knot. 0 = no knot in that row entry.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Knot lands past the target zone — inside the wrong section of the glove
If beyond the piece length, the knot never happens and the row is wasted
high.action: Decrease until the knot lands on the target course from the pattern card.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Knot tied too early — inside the previous section
Multiple close knots make a hard, uncomfortable lump band
low.action: Increase to the exact target course; space knots per the style spec.

items.name: Column — Yarn Number
items.what: Which yarn the knot is tied on — 1 = main yarn, 2 = sub yarn (when fitted). 0 = no knot.

high.title: Wrong yarn number
items: Knot tied on the wrong yarn — it works loose because that yarn is not carried there
A number with no such yarn fitted → alarms or the row is skipped
high.action: Use 1 for knots in the main yarn — the standard case; use 2 only when the style ties off the sub yarn.

items.name: Column — Adjustment
items.what: Fine offset of the knot position around the Knot Row — shifts the tie by a small amount when the knot lands a course or two off target.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Knot drifts past the intended position by the offset amount
Stacked with a wrong Knot Row, pushes the knot into the wrong section
high.action: Return to 0 and correct the Knot Row itself; use Adjustment only for one-course fine tuning.

low.title: Value too LOW (negative)
items: Knot moves before the target course
low.action: Keep at 0 unless a one-course shift is documented on the pattern card.

items.name: All zeros — knotting currently unused
items.what: Every row is 0, so the knotter never fires — consistent with knotting function 0 on page 7. Standard production ties off yarn by overlocking instead of knots.

high.title: Before enabling knots
items: Set knotting function on page 7 to match the number of wraps the style needs
Clean and test the knotter blades on waste yarn first
Enter Knot Row and Yarn Number together, then test one piece at first-run speed
high.action: Knots that slip or jam usually mean dirty knotter blades — clean them before changing table values.

items.name: Blow table — what it does
items.what: Programs exactly where the air blow fires during each piece — each row gives a row range (Start Row → End Row) and whether the blow is ON (1) or OFF (0) inside it. Row 1 is active: the blow fires on rows 3–8; all other rows are 0 and ignored.

high.title: How to read this table
items: Row 1: blow ON from course 3 to course 8 — the machine clears lint and cut ends through the early body of the piece
Rows 1–2 and everything after course 8 get no blow — the cast-on and the wrist/seal area are left alone
Add more rows only if another zone needs its own blow timing
high.action: Keep unused rows at 0; photograph the table before changing it.

items.name: Column — Start Row (set to 3)
items.what: The first course where this blow row becomes active. Set to 3 here so the first two courses — the cast-on — are not disturbed by air.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Blow starts late — lint and yarn ends accumulate in the early courses
If set past the End Row the row never fires
high.action: Decrease toward 3 unless the cast-on proves unstable under blow; rows 1–2 are usually best kept unblown.

low.title: Value too LOW (1–2)
items: Air hits the cast-on — first loops can lift or shift, start becomes unstable
Light yarns blow around and tangle at the very start
low.action: Increase back to 3 if start quality drops after blow changes.

items.name: Column — End Row (set to 8)
items.what: The last course where this blow row stays active.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Blow continues past the intended zone — wasted air, light yarns disturbed near the wrist and seal
high.action: Decrease the End Row until the blow stops where the zone ends.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Only part of the zone is cleared — lint remains and gets knitted in further down
low.action: Increase the End Row until the whole target zone is covered; keep it below the wrist/seal region unless that area needs blowing.

items.name: Column — Blow (1 = ON, 0 = OFF)
items.what: Whether the air blow is ON (1) or OFF (0) inside the row range. Row 1 is ON for rows 3–8.

high.title: ON where it should be OFF
items: Air wastes on zones that do not need it
Very light or hairy yarns fly and tangle; elastic yarns can be pushed off position
high.action: Set 0 for zones that knit light, elastic or already-clean yarn.

low.title: OFF where it should be ON
items: Lint and cut ends accumulate — dropped stitches, dirty-looking fabric, sensor false alarms from debris
low.action: Set 1 with a Start/End range covering exactly the lint-prone courses.

items.name: Why rows 1–2 and the wrist are not blown
items.what: The program blows only courses 3–8. The cast-on (rows 1–2) needs a still start so the first loops seat properly, and the wrist/seal area is handled by the overlock hardware — blowing there disturbs the elastic position more than it helps.

high.title: If you change this pattern
items: Extending blow toward row 1 can destabilise the cast-on — watch the first rows closely
Adding a blow zone near the wrist can move elastic — verify wrist tension after any change
high.action: Treat rows 3–8 as the proven safe window; widen it only after a test piece passes inspection.

items.name: Button — Delete All
items.what: Clears all Start Row, End Row and Blow values in one action. No undo.

high.title: When to use it
items: When switching yarn types — e.g. from a lint-heavy yarn to a clean smooth yarn that needs no programmed blow
Before entering a completely new blow program
high.action: Record row 1 (3–8, ON) before deleting so it can be restored exactly.

items.name: Head location table — what it does
items.what: Programs fine left/right position offsets of the knitting head for specific row ranges of the piece. Each row brackets a range (Start Row → End Row) and shifts the head left or right within it to align pattern features exactly with the physical needles. All values are 0 — no offsets are programmed.

high.title: How to use it
items: Use only when a pattern feature must sit a needle or two off its natural position — e.g. aligning a mark with the seam
Head Left and Head Right are used one at a time per row — a row normally carries a value in only one of them
Keep unused rows at 0
high.action: These are pattern-programmer values — restore from the pattern file or recorded backup after any change, and verify with one test piece.

items.name: Column — Start Row / End Row
items.what: The first and last course where this head-offset row is active — same meaning as in the other tables on pages 2–5.

high.title: Rows wrong
items: Offset starts late — the first courses of the feature sit at the natural position
Offset ends early — only part of the feature is shifted
Overlapping rows with opposite offsets — the head fights itself and alarms
high.action: Bracket exactly the courses of the feature and keep rows non-overlapping.

items.name: Column — Head Left
items.what: Shifts the knitting head to the left by this amount throughout the row range.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Pattern shifts too far left — features misalign to the left of the seam or fingers
Carriage travels closer to its left limit — risk of end-stop crashes on wide pieces
high.action: Decrease the offset; most corrections need only 1–2 steps.

low.title: Value too LOW for the need
items: Feature still sits right of its intended position by the remaining error
low.action: Increase 1 step at a time and check the feature position on a test piece.

items.name: Column — Head Right
items.what: Shifts the knitting head to the right by this amount throughout the row range — the mirror of Head Left.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Pattern shifts too far right — mirrored version of the left-offset faults
Right end-stop crash risk on wide pieces
high.action: Decrease the offset; combine with Head Left only if the pattern documentation says so.

low.title: Value too LOW for the need
items: Feature remains left of its target
low.action: Increase 1 step at a time, verifying on a test piece.

items.name: All zeros — no head offsets
items.what: Every row is 0, so the head knits at its natural position across the whole piece — the normal state for standard patterns.

high.title: When to add offsets
items: Only when a style drawing shows a feature that must sit off the natural needle position
After any head motor, belt, or home-sensor service that could have shifted the reference — restore the recorded offsets instead of re-measuring
high.action: If the whole pattern shifted uniformly, the cause is mechanical (home position) — fix that first instead of patching with this table.

items.name: Button — Delete All
items.what: Clears every Start Row, End Row, Head Left and Head Right value in one action. No undo.

high.title: When to use it
items: When switching back to standard patterns that need no head offset
Before loading a completely new set of offsets
high.action: Photograph or write down any active rows first so they can be restored exactly.

items.name: Slots number
items.what: Number of active knitting slots the control maps for this pattern. It defines how the carriage addresses the needle bed for this glove model.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Set lower than actual — pattern squeezed, fingers and palm misaligned
Set higher than actual — empty slots snag yarn, drop stitches, constant alarms
high.action: Do not tune by trial. Copy this value from the pattern card / spec sheet for this glove model and machine gauge.

items.name: Angle at which the hook blade hooks down
items.what: Cam angle where the overlock hook blade swings down to catch the yarn. Part of the hook trajectory calibration.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Hook misses the yarn — overlock seam does not start
Hook hits the blade or needle — damaged hooks, broken needles
Yarn chewed or frayed at the wrist edge
high.action: Technician calibration only. Restore the recorded value after any hook, blade or cam service — never adjust to chase a quality symptom.

items.name: Angle at which the scissors cut the yarn
items.what: Cam angle at which the scissors close to cut the yarn. Timing must match yarn position exactly.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Yarn not cut — tails drag into the next course
Yarn cut too early — frayed ends, uncaptured tail
high.action: Technician set. Check blade sharpness and clearance first — a dull blade mimics a timing fault.

items.name: Distance run by the fork motor circle
items.what: Travel distance of the yarn-fork servo during its working cycle — how far the fork moves to present the yarn.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Fork stops short — yarn not presented, feeding misses
Fork travels too far — yarn pulled off the feeder or stretched
high.action: Restore from machine records after fork motor or linkage service.

items.name: Distance run by the scissors motor circle
items.what: Travel distance of the scissors servo during its working cycle.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Scissors do not fully close — incomplete cut
Over-travel — mechanical shock, blade damage
high.action: Restore from machine records after scissors motor or linkage service.

items.name: Starting position for releasing elastic yarn
items.what: Servo position where elastic release begins. Together with the ending position it defines how much elastic is fed.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Release starts too early or too late — wrist elastic uneven around the cuff
Together with a wrong end position: elastic too long (loose cuff) or too short (tight cuff)
high.action: Change only together with the ending position as a pair, and verify by measuring the elastic length in the wrist.

items.name: Ending position for releasing elastic yarn
items.what: Servo position where elastic release ends. The fed elastic length = start (262) minus end (240).

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Gap too big — too much elastic, loose wavy cuff
Gap too small — elastic overstretched, tight wrist, snapping elastic
high.action: Adjust in small steps with the starting position; test one glove and check wrist stretch before resuming production.

items.name: Fork alarm deviation
items.what: How far the yarn fork is allowed to drift from its target position before the machine alarms and stops.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Real feeding faults pass unnoticed — missed yarn runs many courses
Gradual mechanical wear silently degrades quality
high.action: Decrease to 3–4 if feeding faults are being missed or quality drifts between checks.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Vibration and normal play trip false alarms
Machine stops repeatedly for no real fault — lost production
low.action: Increase to 6–8 if false fork alarms dominate; clean and tighten the fork mechanism first.

items.name: Depth of front press needle
items.what: How deep the front presser pushes needles into the work during formation and transfer.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Needles bent or hooks damaged
Fabric marks, presser lines on the palm
high.action: Decrease toward 15–16 if needles bend or the palm shows press marks; check presser alignment first.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Skipped stitches and floats — needles not properly pressed
Loops and ladders in the fabric
low.action: Increase toward 18–20 if stitches skip with a healthy presser; verify with a slow first run.

items.name: Depth of rear press needle
items.what: Same press depth setting for the rear bed, used at the palm and half-needle sections.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Bent rear needles — holes appear exactly at the palm taper
Density marks on the back of the glove
high.action: Decrease slightly if rear needles bend or marks show; rear bed is less visible — inspect deliberately.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Rear bed drops stitches — ladders at the small palm
Half-needle sections do not form cleanly
low.action: Increase toward 18–20 if ladders appear at the taper with good needles.

items.name: Oiling interval
items.what: Minutes between automatic lubrication cycles. The machine oils itself on this timer during production.

high.title: Value too HIGH (long interval)
items: Dry needle hooks and cams — noise, heat, premature wear
More needle breakage in long continuous runs
high.action: Decrease toward 90–120 minutes in dusty, hot conditions or with long uninterrupted runs.

low.title: Value too LOW (short interval)
items: Excess oil consumption, oil mist on yarn and floor
Oil stains on light-coloured gloves
low.action: Increase toward 150–180 if oil consumption is high and the environment is clean and cool.

items.name: Oiling time
items.what: How many seconds the oil pump runs at each automatic oiling.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Oil drips and pools — first gloves after oiling show stains
Wasted oil, slippery floor around the machine
high.action: Decrease to 3 s if staining appears; check that oil lines are not blocked causing over-feed at the pump.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Oil does not reach far ends of the needle bed — dry spots
Squeaking or rising noise a few hours after oiling
low.action: Increase to 4–5 s if dry spots or noise return quickly; verify oil level and line flow first.

items.name: Screen off time
items.what: Minutes of no touch before the operator screen dims or sleeps. Display convenience only — does not affect knitting.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Screen stays on — panel wears faster, distractions at night
high.action: Decrease to 1–3 min for panel life; any tap wakes it instantly.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Screen sleeps while the operator is watching production across the room
low.action: Increase to 3–5 min if the screen keeps dimming during normal monitoring.

items.name: Accumulated production
items.what: Lifetime counter of gloves produced by this machine. Information only — used for maintenance scheduling and output tracking.

high.title: How to use it
items: Plan needle, cam and belt replacements against this counter per the maintenance schedule
Sudden resets indicate a control battery or memory issue — record the value daily
high.action: Never edit. Log it at each shift for production records.

items.name: Front press needle unit speed
items.what: Servo speed of the front presser unit — how fast the presser moves into and out of the needles.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Presser overshoots — needle shock, bent needles
Mechanical impact noise, faster wear of the presser cam
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if you hear impact noise or see bent needles with correct depth.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Presser arrives late — stitches skip at high production speed
Cycle time creeps up
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 only if press timing lags at full speed.

items.name: Front density unit speed
items.what: Servo speed of the front density cam — how fast stitch length changes are executed.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Density steps arrive with a snap — visible gauge marks at transitions
Cam mechanism wear
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if marks appear at density change points.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Slow density response — the section ends before density settles
Wrist density does not reach target on short sections
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 if wrist density lags the pattern.

items.name: Rear press needle unit speed
items.what: Servo speed of the rear presser unit — same role as the front presser on the back bed.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Rear needle shock and bending — ladders at the palm taper follow
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if rear needles bend or impact noise comes from the back.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Rear press timing lags — skipped stitches at the half-needle sections
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 only after the rear presser mechanism is confirmed healthy.

items.name: Rear density unit speed
items.what: Servo speed of the rear density cam, controlling back-bed stitch length changes.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Gauge marks on the back of the glove at density transitions
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if back-face marks appear at the wrist or taper.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Rear density lags the pattern — uneven fabric tension, misshaped palm
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 if rear density does not settle within its section.

items.name: Fork motor speed
items.what: Servo speed of the yarn fork — how fast the fork moves to present and withdraw the yarn.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Fork overshoots — yarn thrown off or double-presented
Wear on the fork linkage
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if the fork overshoots or feeding becomes erratic at high speed.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Fork arrives late — yarn presented after the needles pass
Missed feeding at full production speed
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 if feeding misses only appear at maximum speed.

items.name: Scissors motor speed
items.what: Servo speed of the scissors unit — how fast the blades open and close.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Cut happens with shock — yarn pushed away instead of cut, frayed ends
Blade edge chips over time
high.action: Decrease toward 250 if ends fray or the cut timing feels violent.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Blades close too slowly — yarn drags before cutting, tails stretched
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 if cuts are incomplete at high speed with sharp blades.

items.name: Main scissors speed
items.what: Running speed of the main scissors servo during the cut sequence at the wrist.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Cut shock — yarn pulled before it is cut, frayed or stretched tails
Blade and linkage wear increases
high.action: Decrease toward 150–180 if ends fray or the mechanism bangs.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Cut sequence takes too long — wrist section becomes the bottleneck
Yarn can slip out of the blades before they close
low.action: Increase toward 200–250 once cuts are clean at current speed.

items.name: Sub scissors speed
items.what: Running speed of the sub scissors that cut the secondary (sub) yarn.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Sub yarn cut shock — the fine sub yarn frays or slips out of position
high.action: Decrease toward 150–180 if the sub yarn end frays after cutting.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Sub yarn cut lags — it gets carried into the next course and tangles
low.action: Increase toward 200–250 if sub yarn tails appear where they should have been cut.

items.name: Cylinder speed (finger)
items.what: Rotation speed of the pattern cylinder (dial) while knitting the finger sections, where needle selection changes most often.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Cylinder overshoots its target position — wrong needles selected
Finger sections knit with mixed selections — distorted fingers, alarms
high.action: Decrease toward 350 if finger sections show selection errors or cylinder position alarms.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Cylinder cannot complete its rotation within the finger section
Selection runs into the next section — pattern smears across finger roots
low.action: Increase toward 400–450 only if selection timing lags at high speed.

items.name: Cylinder speed (palm)
items.what: Rotation speed of the pattern cylinder while knitting the palm and wrist, where selection changes are less frequent.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Unnecessary shock on the cylinder drive — wear without any speed benefit
Overshoot at the few palm selections that do change
high.action: Keep at or below 300; the palm does not need finger-section speed.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Palm selections lag — density and half-needle selections land one course late
low.action: Increase toward 300–350 if palm selections visibly lag the pattern.

items.name: Front rod sealing position
items.what: Stop position of the front sealing rod — where the rod rests to hold the work during the overlock seal.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Seal forms away from the edge — skipped or floating overlock stitches
Rod presses into the needles — bent needles, marks on the wrist
high.action: Technician set after any rod, bearing or seal-head service. Do not adjust to chase seam quality — check rod wear and alignment first.

items.name: Rear rod sealing position
items.what: Stop position of the rear sealing rod, paired with the front rod during the seal.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Rear support missing during seal — the wrist edge vibrates and the seam skips
Rear rod contacts needles — damage on the back of the wrist edge
high.action: Technician set together with the front rod. The pair must be calibrated as a set.

items.name: Fork homing distance
items.what: Distance the fork servo travels toward its home sensor when finding the reference position at start-up.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Fork cannot find home — machine refuses to start, homing alarms
Fork references against the wrong edge — all feeding positions drift
high.action: Restore the factory value after fork servo, belt or sensor replacement. Never use it to correct feeding symptoms.

items.name: Scissors homing distance
items.what: Distance the scissors servo travels to find its home sensor at start-up.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Scissors homing faults at power-up
All cut positions drift — cuts land early or late across the whole cycle
high.action: Restore the factory value after scissors servo or sensor service.

items.name: Head version
items.what: Hardware version of the knitting head installed on this machine. The control uses it to select correct motion parameters.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Wrong version → head moves with mismatched timings — crashes, mis-knits, alarms
Usually only wrong after a head replacement or control board swap
high.action: Match it to the label on the physical head. If in doubt after a repair, confirm with the technician who did the swap.

items.name: Head homing distance
items.what: Reference approach distance the knitting head uses when finding its home position.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Head homing faults or slow homing at start-up
Head position drifts — pattern start point wanders between pieces
high.action: Restore the factory value after head motor, belt or home-sensor service.

items.name: Cylinder location when knitting first row of little finger with sub yarn set
items.what: Cylinder position offset used for the first little-finger row when sub yarn is active — aligns the sub-yarn selection with that row.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Sub yarn appears one row early or late at the little finger
Reinforced row lands in the wrong place on gloves with sub yarn
high.action: Keep at 0 unless the pattern documentation for a sub-yarn style specifies an offset; restore from pattern file if corrupted.

items.name: Cylinder location when idling the first row
items.what: Cylinder position used during the empty idling rows at the start, before real knitting begins.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Idling rows knit with wrong needle selection — the chain tangles or snags
Transition from idling to first real row is rough — yarn jumps
high.action: Normally never changed. If start-up behaviour changed after a cylinder service, restore the recorded value.

items.name: Sub scissors releasing yarn angle (v0)
items.what: Base angle of the sub scissors when releasing the sub yarn — the starting point of its release motion.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Sub yarn released too early or held too long — tails tangle with main yarn
Sub yarn not released at all — carried into the fabric
high.action: Technician calibration. Only relevant when sub yarn function is in use.

items.name: Main scissors version
items.what: Hardware version of the main scissors unit, telling the control which motion profile to use.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Wrong motion profile — cut timing off, blades strike the hook or plate
Usually only wrong after a scissors unit replacement
high.action: Match it to the label on the installed scissors unit after any replacement.

items.name: Angle of the main scissors when hooked at the highest point (v1, v2)
items.what: Servo angle of the main scissors at the top of its hooked position — the peak of the hook trajectory where it carries the yarn.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Hook carries the yarn too low or too high — yarn slips off or never engages
Scissors strike neighbouring parts at the top of travel
high.action: Technician calibration after scissors servo or mechanical service. Both v1 and v2 must be set as a pair.

items.name: Angle of the main scissors when released yarn (v1, v2)
items.what: Servo angle of the main scissors at the yarn release point — where the hook lets go of the yarn for the cut and seal.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Yarn released too early — drops before the cut, tail hangs loose
Yarn released too late — dragged through the seal, puckered edge
high.action: Technician calibration, set together with the hooked angle as one trajectory.

items.name: Sub scissors version
items.what: Hardware version of the sub scissors unit. Version 0 = the standard/basic sub scissors fitted.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Wrong motion profile for the fitted unit — sub yarn cut timing off
Only wrong after a sub scissors unit swap
high.action: Match to the label on the installed unit after replacement.

items.name: Angle of the sub scissors when hooked at the highest point (v1, v2)
items.what: Servo angle of the sub scissors at the top of its hooked position, carrying the sub yarn.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Sub yarn slips off the hook before the cut — uncut sub yarn tails
Hook strikes parts at the top of travel
high.action: Technician calibration after sub scissors service.

items.name: Angle of the sub scissors when released yarn (v1, v2)
items.what: Servo angle of the sub scissors at the release point — where it lets go of the sub yarn.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Sub yarn dropped early or dragged — tails at the wrong spot in the fabric
high.action: Technician calibration, set together with the hooked angle.

items.name: Broken needle detection signal start (back)
items.what: Starting position of the detection window on the rear bed — where the broken-needle sensor signal begins to be evaluated.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Window starts too late — a broken needle in the first part of the pass is missed
Window too early — normal needle motion triggers false stops
high.action: Technician set. If false trips occur with detection ON, clean the sensor before touching these windows.

items.name: Broken needle detection signal end (back)
items.what: End position of the rear-bed detection window. Together with the start it brackets where broken needles are looked for.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Window ends too early — breaks near the end of the pass are missed
Window too wide — false trips from parts entering the view
high.action: Technician set as a pair with the start position.

items.name: Broken needle detection signal start (front)
items.what: Starting position of the detection window on the front bed.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Same behaviour as the rear window — missed breaks or false trips on the front bed
high.action: Technician set; restore after sensor or carriage service.

items.name: Broken needle detection signal end (front)
items.what: End position of the front-bed detection window.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Front-bed breaks near the end of the pass go undetected
high.action: Technician set as a pair with the front start position.

items.name: Cylinder location during broken needle detection (1)
items.what: Cylinder position reference used during the first half of the broken-needle check — the sensor evaluates needles against this selection state.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Detection compares against the wrong selection state — false broken-needle alarms
Actual broken needles masked by the wrong reference
high.action: Technician set after cylinder or sensor service; never a production tuning value.

items.name: Cylinder location during broken needle detection (2)
items.what: Second cylinder reference position for the second half of the broken-needle check.

high.title: When this value is wrong
items: Same as above — the two reference positions must match the actual selection state during detection
high.action: Technician set; change only together with reference (1).

items.name: Primary and secondary switching solenoid running logic
items.what: Control logic mode for the primary/secondary yarn switching solenoids. 0 = the default switching sequence.

high.title: When to change it
items: Only when the machine documentation for a specific yarn system calls for a different solenoid sequence
A non-zero value here with standard hardware causes switching faults and missed yarn changes
high.action: Keep at 0 for standard setups. Restore after control board or software updates.

items.name: Sub yarn solenoid running logic
items.what: Control logic mode for the sub yarn solenoid. 0 = default sequence for the standard sub yarn feeder.

high.title: When to change it
items: Only per documentation for a non-standard sub yarn feeder
Wrong logic — sub yarn feeds at the wrong time or not at all
high.action: Keep at 0 unless a technician installs a different sub yarn system.

items.name: Tricolor yarn solenoid running logic
items.what: Control logic mode for the tricolor (three-yarn) switching solenoids. 0 = default.

high.title: When to change it
items: Only for machines fitted with the optional tricolor yarn system
Wrong logic — color yarns switch at wrong courses
high.action: Keep at 0 on standard two-yarn machines; this setting does nothing until the option is fitted.

items.name: Languages
items.what: Display language of the operator screen.

high.title: Choosing the language
items: Set to the language your operators read best — menu names must be understood under pressure
Changing language never affects machine behaviour or settings

items.name: Size selection
items.what: Chooses the glove size pattern. The machine adjusts stitch counts and finger shaping so the knitted glove matches the ordered size.

high.title: Choosing the size
items: Set S / M / L / XL exactly per the order sheet — a wrong size is a full batch of rejects
After changing size, run one piece at first-run speed and measure before full production

items.name: Type selection
items.what: Selects the pattern family — General for standard five-finger gloves, or special styles (conjoined, half-finger) that use the extra finger settings on page 3.

high.title: Choosing the type
items: Use General for normal gloves — it ignores the special finger-tip and conjoined-palm settings
Switch type only together with the matching pattern file and size card

items.name: Dropping detection
items.what: When ON, the machine stops if a finished glove does not drop off the needles, preventing it from being knitted into the next glove.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: Turn ON if gloves hang up on needles or you get double-knitted pieces
Turn OFF for normal stable running — lint on the sensor causes false stops

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Fine while dropping is reliable
Check the drop chute and needle condition if stuck gloves appear

items.name: Sub yarn function
items.what: Feeds a second (sub) yarn together with the main yarn to reinforce zones such as the wrist cuff or palm.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: For orders requiring reinforced cuff or palm areas
Remember to also turn ON sub scissors so the sub yarn is cut cleanly

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Normal single-yarn knitting — saves yarn and cycle time
Correct setting for standard gloves

items.name: Overlocking function
items.what: Enables the overlocking head that sews the elastic wrist edge. This must be ON for any glove with a finished elastic wrist.

high.title: When ON (current)
items: Required for all standard finished gloves — do not switch off mid-order
Pair with correct hook/cut yarn laps on page 3

low.title: When to turn it OFF
items: Only for unfinished-cuff pieces or maintenance of the overlock head
If off, the wrist edge unravels — never ship gloves knitted this way

items.name: Knotting function
items.what: Number of wraps the knotter makes to tie the yarn end when changing or finishing. Set to 0, knotting is currently disabled.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Knot becomes bulky and jams at the knotter or needle hooks
Knot visible as a lump inside the glove
Longer cycle time per knot
high.action: Decrease toward 1 or 0 if the knot jams or shows as a defect; check and clean the knotter blades first.

low.title: Value too LOW (or 0 = off)
items: Yarn ends not tied — can unravel at the wrist or seam
Loose tails appear during wearing or washing
low.action: Increase to 1–2 wraps if ends come loose; 0 is fine only when yarn ends are sealed by overlocking instead.

items.name: Blowing function
items.what: Air blow clears cut yarn ends and lint away from the knitting zone and drop area after each piece.

high.title: When ON (current)
items: Keeps needles and sinkers clean — fewer dropped stitches
Essential for dark yarns where lint shows

low.title: When to turn it OFF
items: If air pressure is weak and the blower stalls the cycle
Very light yarns that fly around and tangle with the blow

items.name: Sub scissors function
items.what: Second scissors that cut the sub (second) yarn. Only active when the sub yarn function is used.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: Must be ON whenever sub yarn function is ON — otherwise the sub yarn is never cut and tangles

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Correct for normal single-yarn production

items.name: Cancel half needle function
items.what: Cancels half-needle knitting on the small-palm side. Half needles narrow the little-finger side of the palm for shaping.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: For straight, non-shaped patterns that must not narrow
When half needles are mechanically faulty and you must keep production running temporarily

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Normal shaping is active — palm tapers correctly toward the little finger
Keep OFF for all standard fitted gloves

items.name: Sealing sequence
items.what: Order of operations at the wrist edge — here the yarn is cut first, then sealed (overlocked).

high.title: Choosing the sequence
items: Cut first: clean edge, standard for most yarns — current setting is correct
Seal first: only for slippery yarns that pull back when cut; test one piece before switching

items.name: Main scissors releasing sequence
items.what: How the main scissors release after cutting — successively (one after another) or simultaneously.

high.title: Choosing the sequence
items: Successively: gentler on fine yarns, less shock on the blade — current setting
Simultaneous: faster cycle, use for coarse yarns only

items.name: Distance of half needle on small palm
items.what: Spacing of the half needles on the little-finger side of the palm. Changes how sharply the palm tapers.

high.title: Choosing the distance
items: Short distance: stronger taper, snug little-finger side — current setting
Long distance: straighter palm, roomier fit; switch if gloves feel tight across the palm

items.name: Half needle function of yarn fixing
items.what: Uses the half needles to hold and fix the yarn at the start of a piece, anchoring the first courses.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: When the starting yarn slips and the first rows are loose or ladder
On slippery or elastic-blend yarns that do not grip at cast-on

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Normal cast-on holds fine with the standard yarn

items.name: Head speed when inserting elastic yarn
items.what: Carriage speed while the elastic yarn is being laid into the wrist. It runs slower than normal knitting so the elastic is placed evenly.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Elastic laid loose, wavy or with gaps at the wrist
Missed elastic stitches and uneven tension around the cuff
Higher elastic breakage from snatching
high.action: Decrease toward 100–110 if the elastic line looks wavy or the wrist tension is uneven.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Elastic pulled too tight — stiff, narrow wrist
Elastic feeder drags, elastic snaps frequently
Slower cycle with no quality gain
low.action: Increase toward 130–140 if the wrist is puckered or the elastic keeps snapping from over-stretch.

items.name: Laps of releasing yarn on intact finger
items.what: How many courses of yarn are released (floated) when forming the web next to a normal closed finger.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Weak, loose web between fingers — holes too large
Extra yarn consumption and longer cycle
high.action: Decrease to 1–2 if the web feels flimsy or holes appear at the finger base.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Fingers joined together or web too tight
Stress on yarn at finger separation → breakage
low.action: Increase toward 2–3 if fingers are sticking together or yarn keeps breaking at the web.

items.name: Laps of releasing yarn on hole finger
items.what: Yarn courses released when forming the finger that carries an opening/hole (for styles with a hole or different finger structure).

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Opening too large, edge unsupported
Yarn waste, longer cycle
high.action: Decrease to 2 if the hole edge is loose or oversized.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Hole too small or closes up
Yarn tension spike → snapped yarn at the finger
low.action: Increase to 3–4 if the hole closes or yarn breaks at that finger.

items.name: Rear density value of half needle
items.what: Knitting density on the rear bed where half needles work the small palm. Higher number = tighter fabric.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Small palm too tight — glove fits small, yarn breaks at the taper
Visible density step where half needles engage
high.action: Decrease by 1–2 if the palm side feels tight or yarn breaks at the little-finger base.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Loose, shapeless small palm
Holes or ladders between fingers
low.action: Increase by 1–2 if the small palm looks baggy or shows holes.

items.name: Idling speed
items.what: Speed for running the machine unloaded — used for warm-up after oiling and for clearing lint before production.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Unnecessary wear and heat when running empty
Risk of missed lubrication points on fast dry runs
high.action: Decrease to 120–140 for warm-up runs; idling does not need full speed.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Warm-up takes too long, oil does not reach all points
Ineffective lint clearing
low.action: Increase toward 160 if warm-up cycles run too slowly — never exceed the manual limit for unloaded running.

items.name: Jogging speed
items.what: Inching speed for setup — moving the carriage step by step while fitting needles, checking cams or finding pattern start.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Carriage overshoots position during setup
Danger to hands and tools at the needle bed
high.action: Keep it low — 15–25 is the safe setup band. Never jog fast with hands near the bed.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Setup becomes painfully slow — only a time issue, no quality risk
low.action: Increase slightly to 25–30 if setup feels sluggish, but never trade safety for speed here.

items.name: Reboot speed
items.what: Speed the machine accelerates to right after a restart or reset, before settling into normal production.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Yarn or needle breakage in the first seconds after restart
Missed yarn pickups right after a stop — defects at restart point
high.action: Decrease toward sealing speed (100–120) or add slow restart laps if restarts keep breaking yarn.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Every stop costs more recovery time — lost output across the shift
Long slow stretch before reaching production speed
low.action: Increase toward 120–130 once restarts run clean; match it roughly to sealing speed.

items.name: Sealing speed
items.what: Carriage speed while the wrist edge is being sealed (overlocked). Kept moderate so the overlock head tracks the needles precisely.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Overlock seam skips stitches or misses the edge
Cut elastic, damaged wrist edge, more rejects at inspection
high.action: Decrease to 100–110 if wrist edges show skipped seams or the overlock head mis-tracks.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Wrist section takes too long — bottlenecks the whole cycle
low.action: Increase toward 120–130 only after the seam is confirmed clean at current speed.

items.name: Speed before changing fingers
items.what: Speed the carriage must drop to just before the finger-change mechanism engages, so the cams can shift cleanly.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Finger cams fail to engage — misaligned or stuck fingers
Pattern distortion at the finger roots, machine alarms
high.action: Decrease to 80–100 if you get finger-change faults or misaligned fingers.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Cycle time grows with no quality benefit
low.action: Increase gradually up to 120 once finger changes run fault-free.

items.name: Speed of changing yarn
items.what: Carriage speed during the yarn exchange (transferring knitting from old yarn to new at change or start).

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: New yarn not picked up — float stitches, dropped courses
Knots or tails pulled through the fabric
high.action: Decrease to 60–70 if you see float stitches or missed pickups after a yarn change.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Yarn change drags — time loss only, low quality risk
low.action: Increase toward 90–100 only when every change is confirmed clean.

items.name: Knotting speed
items.what: Speed at which the knotter ties the yarn end. Too fast and the knot is loose or misformed; too slow adds dead time.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Loose, slip-prone knots; knotter misses the wrap
Yarn tail too long inside the glove
high.action: Decrease to 60–70 if knots slip or tails are long.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Knotting station becomes the bottleneck of the cycle
low.action: Increase toward 90 once knots are consistently tight and small.

items.name: Idling laps
items.what: Empty courses the machine knits at start/end with no product, to settle the yarn, clear the feeders and stabilize tension before real knitting.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Wasted yarn and time on every piece
Long loose chain at the start can tangle in the sinkers
high.action: Decrease to 3–4 if starts are stable and yarn cost matters.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: First real courses are loose or uneven — rejects at the cuff
Yarn not yet seated when production starts
low.action: Increase to 5–6 if the first rows show loose stitches or tension wobble.

items.name: First-run speed
items.what: Speed of the very first cycle after loading a pattern or resetting — a verification run to check the pattern forms correctly before full production.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Errors discovered only at full speed — a full batch of bad gloves before anyone notices
Crashing the carriage into a mis-set cam at speed
high.action: Keep it low (30–50). Never raise the first-run speed to save time.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Only cost is a slower verification pass — no quality downside
low.action: No need to increase; if anything, keep this the slowest speed on the machine.

items.name: Speed of releasing elastic yarn
items.what: Speed while the elastic yarn is being released/relaxed at the end of the wrist section, before cut-off.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Elastic released with a snap — tension spike snaps the elastic
Wrist edge puckers after release
high.action: Decrease to 60–70 if elastic snaps at release or the edge puckers.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Release takes too long; elastic may relax unevenly and leave a wavy edge
low.action: Increase toward 90–100 if the edge looks stretched or wavy after release.

items.name: Number of elastic yarn on the end of wrist
items.what: How many elastic threads are knitted into the wrist edge. 1 = standard elastic edge; 2 = stronger, tighter cuff.

high.title: Value too HIGH (2 strands)
items: Wrist too tight — hard to put on, elastic marks on skin
Double elastic cost and more elastic breakage
high.action: Decrease to 1 unless the order explicitly calls for a reinforced elastic wrist.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Wrist edge loose — glove slips off the hand
Cuff rolls over during wear
low.action: Increase to 2 only for orders requiring a firm grip cuff, and lower insert speed accordingly.

items.name: Elastic yarn final release value
items.what: How much tension is released from the elastic right before cut-off — controls how the elastic tail behaves at the final stitch.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Elastic springs back too far — long loose tail at the wrist
Tail sticks out of the overlock seam
high.action: Decrease toward 15–20 if you see loose elastic tails after cutting.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Elastic stays tight at the cut — puckered or gathered edge
Elastic snaps at the cut point from residual tension
low.action: Increase toward 25–30 if the wrist edge puckers or elastic keeps snapping at cut-off.

items.name: Speed after oiling
items.what: Speed the machine returns to after lubrication, paired with the slow-running laps below so oil spreads before full production.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Oil not distributed yet — dry spots wear needles and cams
Oil throw-off contaminates the yarn and fabric
high.action: Keep it at or below 100 until the slow laps are finished; let the laps do their job.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Only delays return to production — no quality benefit
low.action: Once the slow laps complete, the machine can rise to normal speeds automatically.

items.name: Laps of slow running after oiling
items.what: How many slow courses the machine runs after oiling to spread lubricant across the needle bed before speed rises.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Small time loss only — no harm to the machine
high.action: 5 is already generous; 3–4 is enough for daily oiling.

low.title: Value too LOW (or skipped)
items: Oil stays pooled at feed points — dry cams and needle hooks later
Staining on the first gloves from excess oil
low.action: Increase to 5–6 after a full oil service or if the first pieces after oiling show marks or stiffness.

items.name: Needle breakage detection function
items.what: When ON, the machine stops automatically the moment a needle breaks — protecting the needle bed and the fabric.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: When knitting expensive yarns or fine gauges where a broken needle ruins many courses
On night shifts with no operator watching

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Acceptable with an attentive operator and cheap yarn
Turn OFF if dust causes constant false trips — but clean the sensor instead if possible

items.name: Needle breakage detection interval
items.what: How often the breakage detector checks (in courses or seconds, per machine convention). 0 = checking at every cycle / fastest.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Broken needle runs many courses before detection — larger damage
high.action: Decrease toward 0–1 so a break stops the machine almost immediately.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Sensor interrogates constantly — more false trips from lint and vibration
low.action: Increase the interval slightly only if false stops dominate with detection ON.

items.name: Front needle quantity
items.what: Number of needles installed on the front bed for this machine/model. It is a machine specification, not a production setting.

high.title: Never increase
items: More needles than the bed is built for damages cams and carriage
Pattern coordinates all shift — every glove becomes wrong
high.action: Do not change. If this number is wrong, the pattern file or machine model setting is wrong — fix that instead.

low.title: Never decrease
items: Fewer needles narrows the fabric — wrong glove width
Empty needle slots snag yarn and drop stitches
low.action: Do not change. Needle count is set at installation and verified at maintenance.

items.name: Rear needle quantity
items.what: Number of needles on the rear bed — again a fixed machine specification for this model.

high.title: Never increase
items: Same consequences as front bed — mechanical damage and pattern shift
high.action: Do not change; verify only during needle-bed maintenance.

low.title: Never decrease
items: Rear bed gaps cause ladders and holes exactly where half needles work
low.action: Do not change. If gloves show odd holes at the palm taper, inspect needles — do not edit this value.

items.name: Stop main yarn before resetting
items.what: When ON, the main yarn is cut and stopped before the machine resets, so the reset cannot pull loops out of the fabric on the bed.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: When resets keep pulling yarn and dropping courses from the piece on the bed
With slippery yarns that slide under tension

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Fine for normal stops where the piece stays parked correctly
One less cut per reset — slightly less yarn waste

items.name: Laps of three-finger conjoined palm
items.what: Courses knitted in conjoined (joined) structure for the three-finger section of mitten-style patterns. 0 = feature unused.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: On a normal glove this creates a wrongly joined, thick palm section
high.action: Keep at 0 unless running the conjoined pattern type this setting belongs to.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Only wrong when the conjoined pattern IS running — then the joined section is too short
low.action: When running conjoined styles, set per the pattern card for that style.

items.name: Depth of pressing needle (overlocking)
items.what: How deep the overlock presser sinks the needles when forming the wrist seam. 0 = default/standard press depth.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Needles over-bent — breakage and damaged hooks
Wrist seam too tight, fabric puckers
high.action: Decrease toward 0 if overlocking causes needle damage or a gathered seam.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Presser does not form the seam — skipped overlock stitches
Elastic edge not captured, wrist unravels
low.action: Increase in small steps only if the overlock seam skips stitches with a healthy presser.

items.name: Distance of yarn fixing on palm
items.what: Where on the palm the yarn is fixed/tacked during formation. 0 = standard position at the palm base.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Tack point too high on the palm — visible bump or tension mark in the glove body
high.action: Return to 0 unless a specific pattern card calls for a moved tack point.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Yarn fixed too low — insufficient hold, first palm courses loosen
low.action: Leave at 0 for standard patterns; adjust only per pattern documentation.

items.name: Hook yarn laps (overlocking)
items.what: How many wraps the hook yarn takes when catching the wrist edge for overlocking.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Bulky overlock start, yarn build-up at the seam corner
Longer cycle, more yarn
high.action: Decrease to 1 if the seam start is bulky; 1 is standard.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Hook misses or releases the edge — overlock seam does not start
Wrist edge opens after washing
low.action: Increase to 2 only if the seam start repeatedly misses on slippery yarn.

items.name: Cut yarn laps (overlocking)
items.what: Wraps the cutter yarn takes before the final cut at the wrist overlock.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Yarn bundle too thick to cut cleanly — frayed ends
Extra yarn consumption
high.action: Decrease to 1 if the cut end frays; check cutter blade sharpness too.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Cut end slips back and unravels before the overlock captures it
low.action: Increase to 2 if wrist ends unravel before sealing.

items.name: Hide yarn ends function (overlocking)
items.what: Automatically tucks the cut yarn tail into the fabric so the inside of the glove has no loose ends.

high.title: When ON (current)
items: Clean inside finish — no irritation for the wearer
Essential for inspection-passing first-quality gloves

low.title: When to turn it OFF
items: Rarely — only if the hiding action itself marks the fabric on very fine yarns

items.name: Adjusting knitting speed
items.what: Lets the machine slow down automatically in dense/tight sections (like the wrist) where needle load is highest.

high.title: When to turn it ON
items: When knitting dense cuffs at high production speed and needles keep breaking
When the wrist section shows tension marks at full speed

low.title: When OFF (current)
items: Fine when the machine runs comfortably at constant speed
Slightly faster cycle, simpler behaviour

items.name: Density location of hiding yarn ends
items.what: The exact stitch/course coordinate where the yarn-end hiding action happens. It is a pattern-file value, not tuned by hand.

high.title: Wrong value
items: Hide point lands mid-pattern — visible dip or mark on the glove face
Yarn end not hidden at all
high.action: Do not adjust by trial. Restore the value from the original pattern file for this glove model.

low.title: Wrong value
items: Same as above — the coordinate must match the pattern file exactly
low.action: Reload the pattern or re-enter 243 per the pattern card.

items.name: Density value of hiding yarn ends
items.what: Fabric density used at the yarn-hiding point — the machine briefly knits tighter to lock the tail in.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Hide point much tighter than surrounding fabric — visible ring or gauge mark
high.action: Match it to the neighbouring density values (±1–2) if a ring shows.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: Tail not locked — works loose after washing and wear
low.action: Increase toward the local density if tails come out of the fabric.

items.name: Sub/scissors idling movement
items.what: Idle positioning movement of the sub-scissors mechanism. 0 = no idle offset.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Sub scissors sit away from home — slower response, wrong cut timing
high.action: Return to 0 unless the mechanism documentation specifies an offset.

low.title: Value too LOW
items: No issue — 0 is the normal resting setting
low.action: Keep at 0.

items.name: Laps of insert yarn at little finger tip
items.what: Extra reinforcement yarn inserted at the little-finger tip. 0 = off — currently no reinforcement anywhere (all five finger tips are 0).

high.title: Value too HIGH
