items: Tip becomes stiff and thick — uncomfortable, looks different from spec
Extra yarn and cycle time on every piece
high.action: Keep 0 unless the order is for reinforced/wear-resistant gloves; then set per the spec sheet.

low.title: Value too LOW (0)
items: No reinforcement — tips wear through fast on heavy-duty gloves
low.action: For anti-wear orders, set typically 2–4 laps at the specified fingers only, and test one glove for stiffness.

items.name: Laps of insert yarn at ring finger tip
items.what: Same reinforcement setting as the little finger tip, applied to the ring finger.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff, thick tip — mismatch with the other fingers if set unevenly
high.action: Keep all five finger tips at the same value (all 0 for standard gloves, or all set together for reinforced orders).

low.title: Value too LOW (0)
items: Tip unprotected on wear-resistant orders
low.action: Set together with the other fingers per the order spec.

items.name: Laps of insert yarn at middle finger tip
items.what: Same reinforcement setting as the little finger tip, applied to the middle finger.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff, thick tip — mismatch with the other fingers if set unevenly
high.action: Keep all five finger tips at the same value (all 0 for standard gloves, or all set together for reinforced orders).

low.title: Value too LOW (0)
items: Tip unprotected on wear-resistant orders
low.action: Set together with the other fingers per the order spec.

items.name: Laps of insert yarn at index finger tip
items.what: Same reinforcement setting as the little finger tip, applied to the index finger.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff, thick tip — mismatch with the other fingers if set unevenly
high.action: Keep all five finger tips at the same value (all 0 for standard gloves, or all set together for reinforced orders).

low.title: Value too LOW (0)
items: Tip unprotected on wear-resistant orders
low.action: Set together with the other fingers per the order spec.

items.name: Laps of insert yarn at thumb finger tip
items.what: Same reinforcement setting as the little finger tip, applied to the thumb finger.

high.title: Value too HIGH
items: Stiff, thick tip — mismatch with the other fingers if set unevenly
high.action: Keep all five finger tips at the same value (all 0 for standard gloves, or all set together for reinforced orders).

low.title: Value too LOW (0)
items: Tip unprotected on wear-resistant orders
low.action: Set together with the other fingers per the order spec.

tables.caption: Front & Rear density — rows 1–10 (rows 11–20 on Next)

columns.name: Start Row
columns.what: First course where this density applies.
wrong: Too high — tightening starts after the region; if past End Row the row never fires
columns.action: Set it on the first course of the region — smaller than End Row.

columns.name: End Row
columns.what: Last course where this density applies.
wrong: Too high — spills into the next region, overlaps segments
columns.action: End it at the true last course; keep rows non-overlapping.

columns.name: Density Value (Front)
columns.what: Stitch density between Start and End row. Higher = tighter.
wrong: Too high — tight band, glove fits small there, yarn breaks, visible gauge step
columns.action: Lower by 1–2 and re-measure.

columns.name: Start Row (Rear)
columns.what: First course where this rear-bed density applies.
wrong: Too high — tightening starts after the region
columns.action: Set it on the first course of the region.

columns.name: End Row (Rear)
columns.what: Last course where this rear-bed density applies.
wrong: Too high — spills into the next region
columns.action: End it at the true last course.

columns.name: Density Value (Rear)
columns.what: Same for the rear bed. Normally copies the front.
wrong: Too high — back-face marks, rear needles bend
columns.action: Copy front values (Copy All), then adjust only rows meant to differ.

rowNotes.title: Row 1 is the only active density row
rowNotes.what: The first two courses of every piece get table-controlled density — everything after row 2 follows the drawing zone values. Front 7 and rear 10 anchor the cast-on so the start cannot ladder.
high: Front 7 too high — start edge puckers or curls, start yarn breaks
Rear 10 too high — edge curls toward the back
Rear much tighter than front — start skews or twists
rowNotes.highAction: If the start curls or breaks, loosen the front toward 6–7 and keep the rear only 2–4 steps above it.
low: Front 7 too low — first rows loose, ladders at cast-on
Rear 10 too low — start skews, cast-on unstable
rowNotes.lowAction: Raise the rear back toward 10; it should hold the cast-on firmly on both beds.

tables.caption: Sub yarn program — rows 1–10 · all zeros = inactive
cols: Lock Yarn Ends at The Beginning
Lock Yarn Ends at The End

columns.name: Start Row
columns.what: First course of the reinforced zone.
wrong: Starts late — zone begins with single yarn
columns.action: Bracket exactly the zone from the spec sheet.

columns.name: End Row
columns.what: Last course of the reinforced zone.
wrong: Ends early — tail of zone unprotected; overlaps cause double switching
columns.action: End at the true last course; keep segments non-overlapping.

columns.name: Sub Yarn Number
columns.what: Which feeder knits the segment: 1 = first sub yarn, 2 = second (if fitted). 0 = none.
wrong: Feeder number not fitted → alarms, segment never knits
columns.action: Use 1 for the standard feeder; 2 only if a second system is fitted.

columns.name: Lock Yarn Ends at The Beginning
columns.what: Tacks the sub yarn tail at the segment start. 0 = off, 1 = on.
wrong: On when unnecessary — small visible tack, slower cycle
columns.action: Set 1 only where the start is a true beginning of sub yarn use.

columns.name: Lock Yarn Ends at The End
columns.what: Tacks the sub yarn tail at the segment end.
wrong: On when unnecessary — extra tack and time
columns.action: Set 1 on the last segment and wherever the spec requires secured ends.

allZero.t: Whole table is 0 — sub yarn is inactive
allZero.what: No sub yarn is knitted anywhere — consistent with Sub Yarn Function OFF and Sub Scissors Function OFF on the knitting pages. Standard single-yarn production.
h: If a row were half-filled (start but no feeder number) it would do nothing — fill all three columns together
allZero.hd: Before enabling: turn ON sub yarn function AND sub scissors, check the sub yarn path and tension, then enter rows and test one piece at first-run speed.

tables.caption: Knot program — rows 1–10 (rows 11–20 on Next) · all zeros = inactive

columns.name: Knot Row
columns.what: Course where the knotter ties. 0 = no knot.
wrong: Too high — knot lands past the target zone or never fires
columns.action: Enter the exact target course from the pattern card.

columns.name: Yarn Number
columns.what: Which yarn is tied: 1 = main, 2 = sub yarn.
wrong: Wrong yarn — the knot works loose because that yarn is not carried there
columns.action: Use 1 for main-yarn knots — the standard case.

columns.name: Adjustment
columns.what: Fine one-course offset of the knot position.
wrong: Stacked on a wrong Knot Row, pushes the knot into the wrong section
columns.action: Keep 0; correct the Knot Row itself first.

allZero.t: Whole table is 0 — knotting is inactive
allZero.what: The knotter never fires — consistent with Knotting Function 0 on the knitting pages. Standard production ties off yarn by overlocking instead of knots.
h: Knots that slip or jam usually mean dirty knotter blades — clean them before changing values
allZero.hd: Before enabling: set knotting function, test the knotter on waste yarn, then enter Knot Row + Yarn Number together and test one piece.

tables.caption: Blow program — rows 1–10 · row 1 active (rows 3–8, ON)

columns.name: Start Row
columns.what: First course where the blow fires. Set to 3 — rows 1–2 are deliberately not blown.
wrong: Too low (1–2) — air hits the cast-on, loops lift or shift, light yarns tangle
columns.action: Keep 3; decrease only if early-course lint proves the blow must start sooner.

columns.name: End Row
columns.what: Last course where the blow stays on. Set to 8.
wrong: Too high — wasted air, light yarns disturbed near wrist and seal
columns.action: End it where the zone ends.

columns.name: Blow (1 = ON, 0 = OFF)
columns.what: Whether air fires inside the range.
wrong: ON where not needed — yarn flies, elastic pushed off position
columns.action: 1 only for lint-prone ranges; 0 elsewhere.

rowNotes.title: Row 1 is the only active blow row
rowNotes.what: The blow (air jet) fires only on courses 3–8 of each piece — puffing away cut yarn ends and lint from the needles while the early body knits. Rows 1–2 (cast-on) are left still so the first loops seat, and the wrist/seal area is left alone so the elastic is not pushed off position.
high: Start Row below 3 (blowing rows 1–2) — air hits the cast-on: first loops lift or shift, the start becomes unstable, light yarns tangle
End Row above 8 — wasted air, and air near the wrist moves the elastic: cuff tension becomes uneven
Blow left ON where lint does not collect — yarn flies and tangles, elastic pushed off position
rowNotes.highAction: If lint is still knitted in, widen the range one course at a time (never below Start 3) and test a piece. If the cast-on destabilises, raise Start Row back to 3.
low: Start Row above 3 — early courses not blown: cut ends and lint get knitted into the first body rows, dirty marks and dropped stitches appear
End Row below 8 — blow stops before the zone is clean: lint carries into the following courses
Blow set to 0 (OFF) — no cleaning at all: needles collect lint all shift, more skipped stitches and sensor false alarms, stops for cleaning more often
rowNotes.lowAction: If you see lint knitted into the fabric or needles getting dirty fast, lower Start Row toward 3 and/or raise End Row above 8, keep Blow at 1, and run one test piece. Turn Blow OFF (0) only for very light yarns that fly and tangle with air, or when air pressure is too weak.

tables.caption: Head offset program — rows 1–10 · all zeros = natural position

columns.name: Start Row
columns.what: First course where the offset is active.
wrong: Late start — first courses of the feature sit at natural position
columns.action: Bracket exactly the feature courses; rows must not overlap.

columns.name: End Row
columns.what: Last course where the offset is active.
wrong: Early end — only part of the feature shifted; overlaps fight each other
columns.action: End at the true last course of the feature.

columns.name: Head Left
columns.what: Shifts the knitting head left by this amount in the range.
wrong: Too high — feature misaligns left, carriage nears left end-stop on wide pieces
columns.action: Most corrections need only 1–2 steps; decrease if misaligned.

columns.name: Head Right
columns.what: Shifts the knitting head right — mirror of Head Left.
wrong: Too high — feature misaligns right, right end-stop crash risk
columns.action: Use one direction per row; increase 1 step at a time and check a test piece.

allZero.t: Whole table is 0 — head knits at its natural position
allZero.what: No offsets are programmed — the normal state for standard patterns.
h: If the WHOLE pattern shifted uniformly, the cause is mechanical (home position or belt) — fix that first instead of patching with this table
allZero.hd: Add offsets only when a style drawing shows a feature that must sit a needle or two off its natural position; restore recorded offsets after any head service.
